Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard division by total quantity and return ZERO for invoices without lines, as the spec requires.
  Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (the project constant) when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum and round the quotient.
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions for conventions: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the exact pattern: to_money(...) for inputs, round_money(...) for outputs, ZERO as sum seed.
  When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions first; mirroring their conversion/rounding idioms satisfies hidden conventions and review comments.
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in round_money(...). Check the repo's money module for existing helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than inventing rounding logic.

item.title: Mirror existing error codes and validation patterns
item.description: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and validation idioms rather than inventing new ones.
item.content: Before writing validation, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same code strings and message formats. Consistency with sibling functions like issue_invoice/authorize makes hidden tests that assert on error codes pass.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer types
item.description: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so explicitly exclude bool when requiring a positive integer.
item.content: When validating an int parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0. Also reject floats like 1.5 that are not ints.

item.title: Normalize money inputs via to_money before comparing
item.description: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before sign checks so strings/Decimals are handled uniformly.
item.content: Call to_money(unit_price) first, then compare against ZERO for negativity; this reuses existing conversion/rounding and raises the project's invalid_amount error for unparseable input instead of a raw exception.
